prompt: Average session time looked flat, but new users' fell while power users' rose.
tells: new users' fell while power users' rose
why: Averages hide opposite trends. Segment users.
trap: The metric isn't vanity; it needs splitting.

prompt: Conversion is fine on desktop but terrible on phones.
why: Splitting by device shows where the problem is.
trap: It's not a test; it's a breakdown.

prompt: 5% of users create 80% of the content, so the team designs separately for them.
tells: 5% of users create 80% of the content
trap: It's not the job; it's the group.

prompt: Users who signed up in March retain far better than those from the February ad campaign.
tells: than those from the February ad campaign
why: Cohorts are segments by start date and source.
trap: Retention is the metric; the move is segmenting.

prompt: Version B wins overall but loses in every country, because more traffic came from the best-converting country.
why: Mixing segments can reverse results. Look per segment.
trap: The test ran; the overall number misleads.

prompt: Small shops and big companies use the product in completely different ways.
trap: The jobs differ, but the move is splitting them.
